who: Historian of Iowa at Iowa State University; PhD in history, University of Iowa, 1981.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Dorothy Schwieder as a former professor of history at Iowa State University and records her Iowa history publications.
University Archives records her Iowa history teaching at Iowa State from 1966, her Iowa history PhD in 1981, and correspondence with Lisa Ossian (1996–1998) and Peter Hoehnle (2002–2003).

notes: LC identity, institution, research field and correspondence with listed students agree.

who: Historian of East European history at Fordham University, 1944–1961; PhD, Jagiellonian University, 1913.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Oskar Halecki, also called Oscar Halecki, as a historian of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and author of A history of Poland and Borderlands of western civilization.
The scholarly obituary identifies Halecki as Fordham professor of East European history from 1944 to 1961 and records his Jagiellonian doctorate in 1913.
John A. Drobnicki states that Eugene Kusielewicz wrote his 1963 Fordham dissertation on the Teschen question under Oskar Halecki’s guidance.

notes: Exact listed student and dissertation confirm the match despite the dissertation date following retirement.

who: Historian of early China at McGill University; PhD, Princeton University, 1997.

evidence.says: The authority describes Griet Vankeerberghen as an associate professor in McGill’s Department of History and Classical Studies who publishes on Western Han texts.
McGill identifies her as a historian of early and medieval China, with a Princeton PhD in 1997 and graduate supervision in early Chinese history.
The department newsletter names Griet Vankeerberghen as supervisor of Wen-yi Huang’s PhD, Negotiating Boundaries: Cross-Border Migrants in Early Medieval China.

notes: Exact listed student and dissertation, department and field agree.

who: Historian of European cultural and social history, especially Italy, at Brandeis University; DPhil, Oxford.

evidence.says: The authority names Alice A. Kelikian and cites Town and country under fascism (1986), identifying its author as an assistant professor at Brandeis University.
Brandeis identifies Alice Kelikian as associate professor emerita of history, specializing in European cultural, cinematic and social history with emphasis on Italy, and lists an Oxford DPhil.

notes: LC affiliation and university profile agree; the Oxford doctorate matches own_phd.

who: Historian of Russia and the Soviet Union at Ohio State University since 1994; PhD in Russian history, Columbia, 1990.

evidence.says: The candidate’s LC authority identifies David L. Hoffmann as an Ohio State historian of Russia and the Soviet Union with a Columbia PhD in 1990, and records Peasant metropolis and Cultivating the masses.
His university-hosted CV lists Ohio State history appointments continuously from 1994 and a Columbia PhD in Russian history in October 1990.
Ohio State’s faculty page confirms his history appointment, Russian and Soviet specialization, Columbia doctorate in 1990 and the same publications.

notes: Candidate authority, doctorate institution and year, field, and employment during the listed students’ studies agree.

who: Historian of Canadian military and medical history at Wilfrid Laurier University; PhD, University of Western Ontario (Laurier lists 2009).

evidence.says: The authority identifies Mark Osborne Humphries as a Wilfrid Laurier history professor, Dunkley Chair and director of its military studies centre.
Laurier identifies Mark Humphries as a history professor specializing in Canadian history, the First World War and medical history, with a Western Ontario PhD in 2009.
Laurier’s repository identifies Mark Humphries as first advisor and supervisor of Lyndsay Rosenthal’s history PhD, Venus in the Trenches, matching the listed student and title.

notes: Direct supervision and LC affiliation confirm identity. AHA gives the doctorate year as 2008; Laurier gives 2009. The year discrepancy remains unresolved.

who: Historian of Montreal and Quebec socioeconomic and urban history at UQAM; PhD in history, UQAM, 1987.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Joanne Burgess as a professor in UQAM’s history department and records her work on Montreal history.
UQAM’s history faculty profile explicitly lists her supervision of Peggy Roquigny’s 2012 dissertation and Joanne Chagnon’s 2010 dissertation, matching both supplied titles.
The Quebec government biography records a UQAM doctorate in history in 1987 and employment in its history department since 1981.

notes: Two exact listed dissertations, LC affiliation and the doctorate institution and year agree.

who: Historian of colonial Latin America at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill; PhD in history, Harvard, 1993.

evidence.says: The candidate’s authority identifies Kathryn Burns as author of Colonial habits (1999), with the name variant Kathryn Jane Burns.
Duke University Press identifies the author of Colonial Habits as Kathryn Burns, associate professor of history at UNC Chapel Hill.
Erbig’s own posting of his 2015 UNC history dissertation, Imperial Lines, Indigenous Lands, states that it was written under the direction of Kathryn Burns.
The reference biography records a Harvard history PhD in 1993, UNC history employment from 2000, and authorship of Colonial Habits.

notes: The LC work links to the UNC historian; the exact listed dissertation and Harvard doctorate institution and year agree.
